themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 77 THIS WEEK—a 346% spike compared to the 17.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting rapid deterioration in road quality, pothole density, or surface damage across Midwood/Ocean Parkway.
evidence: 77 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 17.2 weekly average (346% increase, z-score: 6.21)
Concurrent spike in street sign damage: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 average (967% spike)
306 total DOB building permits filed in 90 days (229 alterations), suggesting active construction that may be degrading streets
reporting_angles: Map the 77 complaints geographically—is there a corridor or neighborhood cluster being hit hardest?
Interview DOE/DOT about whether construction activity (alteration permits) is linked to the spike

themes_detail.label: Noise and Encampments Emerge Simultaneously
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 47 THIS WEEK (288% above the 12.1 weekly baseline), while encampment complaints hit 4 THIS WEEK (1500% spike from 0.2 average)—signaling possible convergence of quality-of-life deterioration.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk: 47 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.1 weekly average (288% increase, z-score: 7.33)
Encampment complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase, z-score: 5.67)
Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints also spiked 422% last week (15 vs. 2.9 avg), suggesting broader street disorder
reporting_angles: Ground-truth the encampment locations: interview outreach teams, see what services are available
Connect noise spike to specific venues, construction, or street activity—is it related to encampments or independent?

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal & Sanitation Slide
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked 440% last week (27 complaints vs. 5.0 average), and unsanitary conditions remain elevated at 975 complaints over 90 days—indicating waste management or property maintenance failures affecting residents.
evidence: Residential Disposal Complaint spike: 27 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.0 weekly average (440% increase, z-score: 8.63)
Unsanitary Condition remains top complaint category with 975 complaints over 90 days
Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition also spiked 220% last week (4 vs. 1.2 avg), suggesting infrastructure failures
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about collection schedules and capacity in Midwood—are there service gaps?
Survey residents about bin placement, overflow, and rodent activity near affected blocks

themes_detail.label: Fireworks Spike Abated But Worth Tracking
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 7 (2700% above the 0.2 weekly baseline), a record spike now subsided—but the underlying cause and enforcement response warrant investigation given severity of z-score (15.59).
evidence: Illegal Fireworks spike: 7 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (2700% increase, z-score: 15.59)
Spike has subsided since 3 weeks ago, suggesting seasonal or event-driven cause
No concurrent Reddit or local news coverage to explain the spike
reporting_angles: NYPD records: were there arrests, enforcement actions, or seized fireworks during that week?
Community context: was there an event, holiday, or gathering that triggered the spike?

themes_detail.label: Multiple Rezonings in Public Review Phase
themes_detail.summary: Five major land-use applications are in active review (2 historic district designations in City Council review, 3 rezonings at varying stages), signaling potential zoning conflicts, displacement concerns, or development pressure that may affect Midwood/Ocean Parkway residents.
evidence: Ditmas Park West & Beverley Square West Historic District designations in City Council review
Three active ULURP rezonings: Coney Island Ave, Nostrand Ave, Flatbush Ave
306 DOB permits filed in 90 days (229 alterations, 30 new buildings), indicating construction uptick
reporting_angles: Interview community board members on historic district designations—are residents supportive or concerned about constraints?
Map the 3 rezonings: who are the applicants, what is the proposed use, how does it align with neighborhood character?
